_meta.title: Life of a 911 - per-stop geometry & visible design features
_meta.schema: Each leaf fact is {value, sources[], note?}. value may be null when nothing was found (note says where we looked). sources are URLs fetched during this research session. Groups: dimensions_mm, overhang_mm, other_published, wheels, headlights, front, rear, rear_spoiler, engine_lid_grille, body, lighting_signature, distinctive[], changes_from_previous_stop[], open_questions[]. 'blueprints' points to research/blueprints/<stop>/sources.json.
_meta.reference_body: Coupe for every stop (see reference_variant per stop).
_meta.method: Researched per era by parallel research agents from Porsche newsroom/press kits/brochures, Porsche Classic pages, period brochures (auto-brochures.com, stuttcars.com), auto-motor-und-sport and Excellence spec sheets, Wikipedia and auction/club sources; photos were viewed to confirm visible features. Where sources disagree the note lists each value and the recommended one.

00-t7-1959.stop_name: Porsche Type 754 T7 (a.k.a. Type 695 / 'T7 prototype') - F. A. 'Butzi' Porsche four-seat design study for the 356 successor

production_years.value: 1959 design model / full-scale mock-up; 1960-61 drivable one-off prototype (not a production car)
production_years.note: Porsche Newsroom: F. A. Porsche 'produced a model of a coupe' in 1959 and 'the prototype 754 was created in 1960 as a highly promising four-seater study'. Wikipedia infobox: 'Production 1961'. Car and Driver: 'the full-scale mockup of the car was cobbled together in the waning days of 1959'. Porsche Museum plaque (#301) dates it 1959.

reference_variant.value: The single surviving T7 prototype in the Porsche Museum, Stuttgart (green metallic, as displayed 2009-2013)

length.note: not published (checked: Porsche Newsroom 754->901 article, Wikipedia Typ 754 T7, Car and Driver, Motor1, PCA archive, Porsche Museum plaque). ESTIMATE ~4,060-4,200 mm: Motor1 studio side photo L/WB = 1798/1031 px = 1.744 x WB 2,330 = ~4,064 mm, plus a few % for perspective at the bumper extremes.

width.note: not found in: Porsche Newsroom, Wikipedia, Car and Driver, Motor1, PCA archive, museum plaque

height.note: not published. ESTIMATE ~1,260 mm (+-60): Motor1 studio side photo roof-to-ground 556 px / WB 1031 px x 2,330.

wheelbase.note: DERIVED photo measurement (recommended value). Rim-flange calibration from the Porsche Museum studio side photo of 901 No. 57 (WB 2211 mm = 1585.5 px, 15-in rim flange 298 px -> 415.6 mm). T7: Motor1 studio side photo WB 1031 px / rim 185 px = 5.57 -> ~2,316 mm; Commons 'Projet T7' (Retromobile 2013, Panasonic FZ8, 36 mm-equiv.) WB 1087 px / rim 192.5 px = 5.65 -> ~2,347 mm. Assumes the T7 runs 15-in rims like the 356/901 (same slotted steel-wheel style; rim size itself not documented). Published claims conflict: Porsche Newsroom 'the 2.40-metre wheelbase from the previous design was shortened to 2.20 metres' (2,400); Wikipedia/PCA/Motor1 '100 mm longer than the 356' (356 = 2,100 mm per Wikipedia -> 2,200). Photos exclude 2,200; 2,400 is ~3% above both photo estimates.

open_questions: Documentation sufficiency: ~17 CC-licensed Commons photos (front, rear, 3/4, near-side views; Category:Porsche_754_T7), Motor1 gallery incl. a clean studio side and front view, and 2 Porsche archive B/W photos - enough for a loose model, but NO published length/width/height/track and NO orthographic drawing. Recommend including T7 only as an approximate 'pre-history' morph source, or skipping it.
Wheelbase conflict: 2,400 mm (Porsche Newsroom) vs 2,200 mm (Wikipedia/PCA/Motor1); photo measurement ~2,330 mm (assumes 15-in rims).

01-901-1963.stop_name: Porsche 901 - prototype / pre-series car of the 1963 IAA Frankfurt world premiere (12 Sep 1963)

production_years.value: Shown 12 Sep 1963 (IAA, pre-series car); first prototype driven 9 Nov 1962; series production of the 901 from 14 Sep 1964; renamed 911 on 22 Oct 1964; 82 cars built as '901'

reference_variant.value: 1963 IAA / press pre-series 901 as specified in the English '901' brochure W 221 e printed 9.63 (Sept 1963); period photos of the yellow 'TYP 901' car and the white 'S-CU 902' prototype. (Production 901s built Sep-Nov 1964, e.g. museum car No. 57, are covered under stop 02 features.)

length.note: 901 brochure 9.63: 'Overall length 4135 mm (162.8 in.)'. (Newsroom 'I Am Legend' gives 164.2 in = 4171 mm for 'the 901' - later/rounded figure.)

width.note: 'Overall width 1600 mm (62.99 in.)'; Newsroom 'I Am Legend': 63.4 in (1610 mm)

height.note: 'Overall height 1273 mm (50.12 in.)'; Newsroom 'I Am Legend': 51.9 in (1318 mm). The 1963 sketch measures ~1270 mm roof-to-ground, i.e. matches 1273.

front.note: DERIVED from the official Porsche 'Sketch, Porsche 911, 1963' side elevation (Newsroom media package, saved as blueprints/01-901-1963/official_porsche_sketch_1963_side.jpg): wheel-centre lines at x=925/2332 px (wheelbase 1407 px), extremes over front/rear bumper guards x=335/2998 px (2663 px). Front share of overhang = 590/1256 px, rear 666/1256 px. Published overhang sum 4135-2204 = 1931 mm split 590:666 -> front 907 mm (+-15 mm). (Sketch alone, scaled by WB: 924 mm.)

rear.note: DERIVED from the official Porsche 'Sketch, Porsche 911, 1963' side elevation (Newsroom media package, saved as blueprints/01-901-1963/official_porsche_sketch_1963_side.jpg): wheel-centre lines at x=925/2332 px (wheelbase 1407 px), extremes over front/rear bumper guards x=335/2998 px (2663 px). Front share of overhang = 590/1256 px, rear 666/1256 px. -> rear 1024 mm (+-15 mm). Sketch WB/L ratio 0.528 vs brochure 0.533 (1% agreement).

curb_weight_kg.note: DERIVED: brochure 'Weight/power ratio (ready to operate) 7.7 kg/HP (DIN)' x 130 HP = ~1001 kg

drag_cd.note: not found in: 901 brochure 9.63, Newsroom 754->901 and 'I Am Legend' articles

windshield_rake_deg.note: DERIVED: windscreen outer line in the 1963 side sketch runs from (1250,1191) to (1565,969) px = ~35 deg above horizontal (~55 deg from vertical), +-2 deg. Not a published figure.

roof_peak_position.value: ~1306 mm behind front axle (59% of wheelbase), ~1270 mm above ground
roof_peak_position.note: DERIVED from 1963 side sketch (roof peak x=1739-1773 px, y=954 px; ground y=1762 px)

design_name.value: Steel disc wheel with a ring of ventilation slots + large domed chrome 356-style hubcap

badging.value: gold 'Porsche' script on the engine lid ('Porsche Schriftzug goldfarben'); '901' rear badge letters had already been made when Peugeot objected

design.value: chrome ventilation grille with horizontal bars at the top of the engine lid (also visible from the side as a louvred patch)
design.note: Porsche Classic (DE): 'Heckdeckel mit verchromtem Lueftungsgitter' (EN page: 'Bonnet lid with chrome-plated ventilation grille')

mirrors.value: round, chrome-plated exterior mirror on the front of the driver's door

door_handles.value: chrome pull handle with push button

side_windows.value: chrome-framed door glass with pivoting front vent window
side_windows.note: brochure: 'larger window areas have been provided'

quarter_window.value: large rear side window with chrome frame, curved rear edge following the fastback

roofline.value: 2+2 fastback ('hatchback with a large rear window')

fuel_filler.value: round flap on top of the left front wing

chrome_trim.value: chrome bumper strips, window frames, sill strip, hubcaps, engine-lid grille

other.value: Body 120 mm longer than the 356 but 70 mm narrower; 'short overhangs'

lighting_signature.value: Round chrome-ringed headlamps in the wing tunnels; below each a slatted chrome horn grille + clear/amber corner lamp; small rectangular corner taillights on the rear bumper

distinctive.value: Pre-series proportions: 28 mm shorter, 10 mm narrower and 47 mm lower (published) than the 1965 production 911, wheelbase 7 mm shorter, ground clearance 118 vs 150 mm
Clean front bumper without guards and without fog lamps on the 1963 cars

changes_from_previous_stop.value: Greenhouse: T7 four-seat notchback with wrap-around rear glass -> 2+2 fastback with large sloping rear window
Wheelbase shortened (Newsroom: 2.40 m -> 2.20 m; 901 brochure: 2,204 mm)
Engine lid gains a slatted chrome grille; T7 relied on small side vents
Front end essentially carried over (T7 front 'could easily be mistaken for its production successor'); the T7's two dark intake openings under the bumper are not seen on the 1963 901 photos
Exterior mirror moves from a stalk on the front wing (T7) to the front of the door (901)

Tail: T7 flat tail with rear-flank intake grilles, black guards around a mesh centre panel and twin centre exhausts -> 901 sloping fastback engine lid with top chrome grille, slim chrome-strip bumper and a single left-hand tailpipe
Side glass: T7's long rear side window (four seats) -> shorter 2+2 quarter window with curved trailing edge

open_questions: Whether the IAA stand car itself carried a '901' script on the engine lid (letters were made per Newsroom) - no rear photo of the stand car found.
Rear lamps/bumper guards of the 1963 show car not visible in any fetched rear photo; modelled from the 1963 sketch + brochure painting.

02-911-swb-1964.stop_name: 911 2.0 Coupe, short wheelbase (O-series MY1965-67, A-series MY1968)

03-911-lwb-1969.stop_name: 911 long-wheelbase Coupé, B/C/D/E/F series (MY1969-MY1973), 2.0 / 2.2 / 2.4 litre, T / E / S

production_years.value: MY1969 (B series, built from mid/Aug 1968) to MY1973 (F series, ended July 1973)
production_years.note: Porsche press release: 'in the middle of 1968: from the 1969 model year, the wheelbase ... grew by 57 millimetres'. G-series production began Aug 1973 (press kit).

reference_variant.value: 1972 911 S 2.4 Coupé (E series, MY1972) - numbers below are for this car unless noted
reference_variant.note: Chosen because Porsche's own 1972 brochure documents its body equipment (front-apron spoiler, chrome sill strips, light-alloy wheels) and photos. Caveat: MY1972 is the only year with the oil-filler flap on the right rear wing; for a 'generic' LWB car omit that flap (MY1969-71 and MY1973 had none).

length.note: Excellence 1972 911 S Coupé: 4,147 mm. Porsche press kit: the G-series body (4,291 mm) was '144 mm longer than its forerunner' -> 4,147 mm. Recommended 4,147 for the 1972-73 911 S.

height.note: Unladen; source does not state load condition.
